headline: CHINA'S Rare Earth Grip 'Tighter Than OPEC's Ever Was,' CEO Warns After Trump-Xi Summit
snippet: The CEO of Real Alloys argues that China's control over 85-90% of global rare earth refining is structurally tighter than OPEC's oil monopoly ever was — a warning that emerged from Trump-Xi summit commentary even as Beijing pledged cooperation. Unlike oil, rare earth processing capacity took decades to build and cannot be redirected in months, making the choke point effectively permanent.

headline: NEXGEN ENERGY Begins Construction This Summer on Canada's Largest-Ever Uranium Mine
snippet: NexGen Energy (TSX/NYSE: NXE) is commencing construction this summer on the Rook I uranium mine in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin — the largest development-stage uranium deposit in Canada. At peak, the project is expected to produce up to 30 million lb U3O8 annually, roughly 20% of current global fuel supply, after a four-year build that will employ 490 people at full operation.

headline: COT REPORT May 22: Gold Shorts Grip the $4,500 Level While Silver Managed Money Rebuilds
snippet: The May 22 Commitment of Traders report shows commercial short pressure continuing to cap gold near the $4,500 level, while silver's managed-money net long position is slowly rebuilding after the January correction from $121/oz. USDX futures positioning offers mixed signals heading into the summer consolidation period for precious metals.

headline: SILVER and Platinum Decouple From Gold as US-Iran War Tightens Industrial Metal Supply Chains
snippet: Silver and platinum are increasingly trading on industrial supply fundamentals — not just safe-haven flows — as the ongoing US-Iran conflict restricts sulfur availability critical to base and precious metal refining. The gold-to-silver ratio has compressed to 59.4, near its tightest level in months, a signal that historically precedes broader strength in the precious metals complex.

headline: 400% IN A WEEK: Highland Critical Minerals Tops TSX-V Gainers on Lithium-Gold Exploration
snippet: Highland Critical Minerals (CSE: HLND) surged 400% to lead this week's TSX-V and CSE gainers, drawing speculative attention to its northern Ontario lithium and Nunavut gold exploration assets. The move sharply reverses a collapse from a C$5.82 November 2025 peak to C$0.20, following a C$400,000 flow-through placement at C$0.25/share in April.

headline: ASX WEEKLY: Canadian Phosphate Rockets 56% After Securing British Columbia Exploration Permit
snippet: Canadian Phosphate (ASX: CP8) surged 55.84% this week after securing an Exploration Permit for its 100%-owned Wapiti Phosphate Project in British Columbia, with drilling commencing immediately to advance a maiden JORC resource estimate targeted for late 2026. Phosphate's critical mineral designation is drawing fresh investor interest amid fertilizer security concerns.

headline: Scorpio Gold Drills 2.68 g/t GOLD Over 11 Metres from Surface at Nevada's Manhattan Project
snippet: Scorpio Gold (OTC: SRCRF) intercepted 11.34 metres at 2.68 g/t gold from 0.7 metres depth at its Manhattan District Project in Nevada, linking exploration targets along the Zanzibar Trend beyond the existing inferred resource pit. The near-surface oxide intercept — accompanied by 23.2 metres at 0.69 g/t from just 4 metres depth in an adjacent hole — strengthens the case for a materially expanded open-pit resource.

headline: Will USA Rare Earth's $2.8 BILLION Serra Verde Deal Actually Break China's Magnetic Rare Earth Monopoly?
snippet: USA Rare Earth's (NASDAQ: USAR) $2.8 billion acquisition of Brazil's Serra Verde — the only mine outside Asia capable of producing all four magnetic rare earths at scale — has analysts divided on whether it can meaningfully offset China's grip on downstream refining and processing. The deal carries a U.S. government-backed 15-year offtake agreement for 100% of Phase 1 NdPr, Dy, and Tb production, but critics note processing infrastructure remains the harder problem to solve.

headline: GOLD'S NEXT CRISIS TRADE: Safe-Haven Demand and Sovereign Debt Risk Drive 2026 Price Outlook
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis argues that gold's structural bull case rests on escalating sovereign debt risk, persistent central bank buying, and renewed geopolitical demand — not just inflation hedging. With gold holding near $4,523/oz after pulling back 19% from its January $5,589 all-time high, the piece frames current consolidation as institutional accumulation ahead of the next leg higher.

headline: HERE'S WHERE GOLD AND SILVER STAND: $4,523 Gold Holds Key Support, Silver Rebuilds Base at $76
snippet: A current-state precious metals summary places gold's hold above $4,500 in context of a 19% correction from January's $5,589 all-time high, while silver at $76.11/oz is showing relative strength with the gold/silver ratio compressing to 59.4x — near its tightest in months. The analysis highlights the $4,400-4,500 zone as the critical band where long-term institutional buyers are reported to be accumulating.
